headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, yet whales are pulling BTC off exchanges as the crowd reads extreme fear
paragraphs: Start with the trend map, because it is unanimous today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day averages, and none carries a golden cross. That is a bear regime by structure, not by mood. The depth varies a lot though. BTC is 48.5% off its 12-month high, ETH 61.1% off, and the small end of the board is far worse: DOGE -75.7%, ADA -80.0%. When every asset sits under its long-term trendline but the damage ranges from moderate to severe, dispersion inside the drawdown is the story, not the drawdown itself.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, because it does not agree with the trend picture everywhere. BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP have RSIs clustered in the high-40s to low-50s and MACD still under signal, essentially flat, resting momentum inside a downtrend. BNB, DOGE and ADA have flipped MACD above signal despite also sitting under their 200-day lines. ADA is the standout: RSI 67.1, up 17% over seven days and 21.8% over thirty, with MACD confirming the short-term push, all while it remains 80% below its yearly high and under its long-term average. That is a real divergence: strong near-term momentum fighting a trend that has not turned.

Positioning tells a mixed story by asset. BTC funding is essentially flat at -0.1% annualized with a long/short ratio of 1.35, cheap and not crowded. ETH funding is meaningfully negative at -6.0% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs to stay short, yet in the last 23 hours ETH shorts absorbed $5.1M in liquidations versus $2.0M for longs, a short squeeze despite the negative funding print. BTC shows the same pattern in miniature: $4.2M in short liquidations against $653K in longs. Meanwhile SOL, XRP and DOGE carry positive funding (7.4%, 4.7%, 7.0% annualized) and long/short ratios running from 2.55 up to 4.87, crowded long books that are the more fragile kind of positioning, expensive to hold and exposed if price stalls.

On flows, the BTC spot ETFs posted a net $21.6M on 04 Aug 2026, and the five-session net is +$191.5M, though same_direction_days of just 2 means that total was not built on a clean run, it is a net positive across a choppy week. ETH ETFs are thinner and weaker: +$1.3M on the day against a five-session net of -$21.7M. On the whale side, $185.9M moved off exchanges net over the last 24 hours, all attributed to BTC, while the two biggest onto-exchange moves were stablecoins: $119.9M in USDC into Coinbase Institutional and $102.8M in USDT into Bitfinex. That is cash arriving at venues while coin leaves them, a combination usually read as accumulation setup. The weekly whale series backs this up in shape if not magnitude: after two days near -$130M to -$135M, the last two prints jumped to roughly +$1.03B each, a sharp swing toward exchange outflows very recently. Stablecoin float itself is down 0.86% over 30 days, so the dry powder pile has shrunk a touch even as some of it moves toward exchanges today.

All of this sits under a Fear & Greed reading of 25, Extreme Fear, which is near the bottom of its own 30-day range of 20 to 33. The crowd's temperature and the tape's behavior are not fully aligned: sentiment is fearful, but BTC ETF flows are net positive over five sessions, whale BTC balances are leaving exchanges, and short positions have taken the bigger liquidation hit in both BTC and ETH over the last day. None of that erases the fact that every major remains under its 200-day line. Worth watching from here: whether the ETF same_direction_days count extends past two, whether the whale weekly net holds its recent swing toward outflows or reverts toward the negative prints seen two days ago, and whether any major asset reclaims its 200-day average, which would be the first structural change to a lineup that is currently seven-for-seven below trend.
